brief.descriptor: B2B software and services company, Illinois

financialPulse: Mid-market software firms are being pushed to show efficient growth, so marketing spend now has to prove pipeline, not just volume.
Customer acquisition costs are rising in crowded categories, which puts more weight on expansion revenue from the installed base.
Boards at this size expect a clear line from content and campaigns to closed revenue, often before approving new hires.
strategicPriorities: Turn the website into a stronger pipeline source with account-aware journeys for target buying teams.
Connect marketing, sales and product usage signals so expansion opportunities surface earlier.
Scale content production without adding headcount, while keeping brand and messaging consistent.
platformPosition: Runs Buying Groups as its largest investment, with CMS, DAM and AB Testing around it: a solid web and B2B marketing core.
That footprint makes account-based journeys and data-driven personalization the natural next step.
Main whitespace: no Data, CDP, Analytics or ESP B2B, so buying-group signals stop at the marketing automation layer.
Partner coverage: Best Strategy is attached and can lead data and journey work.

executives.name: Dana Whitlock
executives.agenda: Pipeline sourced by marketing, cost per opportunity, and win rates on target accounts.
executives.platformAngle: ESP B2B and CDP turn buying-group activity into coordinated journeys sales can act on.
executives.openingHook: Your buying-group scores stop at the inbox. What if every touchpoint used them?
executives.proofPoint: B2B teams that orchestrate journeys by buying group typically see faster stage progression on target accounts.

executives.name: Marcus Ellery
executives.agenda: Net revenue retention, expansion bookings and forecast accuracy across new and existing customers.
executives.platformAngle: Data and Analytics join product usage with marketing and sales activity to flag expansion early.
executives.openingHook: Which accounts are ready to expand this quarter, and how early can your team see it?
executives.proofPoint: Revenue teams with a unified account view usually catch expansion and churn signals a quarter sooner.

executives.name: Priya Kalvani
executives.agenda: Fewer point tools, clean data governance and lower integration effort across the go-to-market stack.
executives.platformAngle: Data gives one governed customer foundation that CDP, Analytics and ESP B2B all share.
executives.openingHook: How many systems hold a different version of the same customer today?
executives.proofPoint: Consolidating customer data onto one governed foundation commonly cuts integration work and reporting disputes.

executives.name: Rafael Ostrander
executives.agenda: Website conversion, content velocity and the time it takes to launch a campaign page.
executives.platformAngle: Digital Optimizer and Content Measure scale on-brand variations on the CMS and DAM they already run.
executives.openingHook: Your team already owns the CMS and DAM. How long does one personalized page take today?
executives.proofPoint: Teams that generate on-brand variations from an existing DAM usually ship personalized pages in days instead of weeks.

slide3.partnerPlay: Run this with Best Strategy. Best Strategy leads the data and journey work: standing up Data and CDP, connecting the Buying Groups instance to the CMS, and building the first account-based journeys in ESP B2B. They also run the analytics workshop that defines which buying-group signals sales sees. The platform team covers licensing, roadmap sessions and executive alignment, while Best Strategy owns delivery and the quarterly optimization cadence after launch.

priorityPlay.theirProblem: Buying-group scores live in marketing automation, but nothing coordinates the journey across email, web and sales outreach for the whole buying team.
priorityPlay.whyThisProduct: ESP B2B orchestrates journeys at the account and buying-group level, using the Buying Groups data they already maintain.
fitSignals: You already score buying groups. ESP B2B makes those scores drive the next message for every member.
Start with one product line and one segment, then expand once sales sees the lift.
priorityPlay.firstMove: Book a working session with marketing operations to map one target segment's buying group and its current touchpoints.
priorityPlay.watchOut: Sales has to agree on the buying-group roles first, or the journeys will target the wrong people.

sellNow.theirProblem: Web, campaign and product signals sit in separate reports, so nobody sees the full path to a deal.
sellNow.firstMove: Offer a two-week analytics assessment on the top three conversion paths.
sellNow.whyWinnable: Low lift to start, and it makes the CMS and AB Testing investments easier to prove.

sellNow.theirProblem: The content team cannot tell which assets in the DAM actually move pipeline.
sellNow.firstMove: Show content performance on their top 20 DAM assets in a one-hour demo.
sellNow.whyWinnable: Extends the DAM they already run and answers a question the CMO is already asking.

sellNow.theirProblem: Event and trial sign-ups use generic forms that do not feed buying-group data back cleanly.
sellNow.firstMove: Rebuild one high-traffic sign-up form as a pilot and connect it to Buying Groups.
sellNow.whyWinnable: Small, fast win that improves data quality for every other play.

millionPlays.name: Account-based revenue engine
millionPlays.theirProblem: Marketing generates leads, but target accounts do not progress because the buying team is not engaged as a group.

products.why: Orchestrates journeys for the whole buying group.
Builds account audiences from every signal in real time.
Unifies account, contact and engagement data.
Shows which journeys move accounts through stages.

millionPlays.partnerScope: Best Strategy implements Data and CDP, builds the first ten journeys, and runs quarterly optimization.
whatHasToBeTrue: Sales and marketing agree on buying-group roles and stage definitions.
Marketing operations can dedicate an owner to journey design.
millionPlays.firstMeeting: Meet the CMO with marketing operations to map one target segment's buying group and agree on stage definitions.

millionPlays.name: Expansion and retention signals
millionPlays.theirProblem: Expansion and churn risk show up too late because product usage, support and marketing data never meet.

products.why: Brings product usage and account data together.
Surfaces expansion and risk patterns by account.
Runs adoption and renewal journeys for end users.

millionPlays.partnerScope: Best Strategy connects product usage data and builds the expansion and risk dashboards.
whatHasToBeTrue: Product usage data can be shared with marketing systems.
The revenue team commits to acting on account alerts each week.
millionPlays.firstMeeting: Meet the CRO and the head of customer success to agree on three expansion signals worth acting on.

millionPlays.name: Personalized web at scale
millionPlays.theirProblem: The website treats every visitor the same, and producing personalized pages takes weeks of design and build time.

products.why: Generates on-brand page and asset variations from the DAM.
Decides which variation each account sees.

millionPlays.partnerScope: Best Strategy builds the personalization framework on the existing CMS and trains the content team.
whatHasToBeTrue: Brand guidelines are documented well enough to drive variations.
The web team can run tests on the highest-traffic pages each sprint.
millionPlays.firstMeeting: Meet the VP of Digital Experience and the content lead to pick the three pages where personalization would matter most.
